sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Recent terrorist attacks in Turkey, Sydney and Indonesia close to home, are growing concerns, especially for Singapore being small and strategically situated.

sections.label: French attack hospital resources
sections.summary: In the French attack, APHP coordinated 40 government hospitals, 100,000 healthcare personnel, 22,000 beds and 20 major operating theatres, numbers beyond Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In the French attack, the Assistance Publique-Hopitaux de Paris (APHP) coordinated 40 government hospitals, 100,000 healthcare personnel, 22,000 beds and 20 major operating theatres – the numbers are really beyond Singapore.

sections.label: Total Defence and social resilience
sections.summary: Border control, maximising the Armed Forces in counter-terror efforts, and nurturing community awareness and social resilience through Total Defence outreach are needed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Others would include our border control, how to maximise our nation's relatively small Armed Forces in counter-terror efforts and also not forgetting, nurturing community awareness and social resilience through our Total Defence outreach and approaches.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We have to look after and look out for one another.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: No one else is going to do this for us, for this is our only country and this will also be our future together.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The future of us, the future of our children and the future of our grandchildren, lie in our hands, as a community, as a society, as a multiracial nation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The only upper limit there is, is the one that is set by our own mindsets.

sections.label: Progress from hard work and planning
sections.summary: Progress results from hard work, careful planning and team effort, not luck, star alignment or mumbo-jumbo.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The progress you see today is the result of hard work and careful planning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is a team effort." Mdm Speaker, it was no luck of the planets, no alignment of stars and no "mumbo-jumbo" that brought Singapore to where it is today but pure hard work, careful planning and more importantly, it was and still is a team effort.

sections.label: Trust built Singapore's rise
sections.summary: Singapore's 50-year rise from Third World to First World was built on Singaporeans' trust in the Government they elected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Our stellar 50-year rise from Third World to First World was built on the trust of Singaporeans in the Government they elected to represent them.

sections.label: Social compact delivered infrastructure
sections.summary: The social compact delivered infrastructure, housing, education, healthcare and social security that catapulted Singapore into First World nations within 50 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: No star-gazing is required to tell us that that social compact delivered excellent infrastructure, housing, education, healthcare, social security that catapulted Singapore into the league of First World nations, all within 50 years.

sections.label: Stars of democracy and equality
sections.summary: The stars are democracy, peace, progress, justice and equality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The stars of democracy, peace, progress, justice and equality.

sections.label: Ethnic Integration Policy discussion
sections.summary: The passage says reaching equality and racial harmony may require mature discussions on sacred cows such as the Ethnic Integration Policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: If we truly believe in reaching equality and upholding racial harmony then perhaps we need mature discussions on sacred cows such as, even the Ethnic Integration Policy.

sections.label: Moving to societal centre
sections.summary: The passage says this is moving to the centre of majority society, and a popular but bankrupt Government is of no use to the people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This is not so much leaning towards the left but moving ourselves to the centre of the majority of society, where societal views may have shifted over the years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We all need to acknowledge at the same time that a popular but bankrupt Government is of no use to the people.

sections.label: Economic progress as cornerstone
sections.summary: The passage says economic progress remains a cornerstone for Singapore's future, handled by Heng Swee Keat's Committee on the Future Economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Economic progress will still be a cornerstone for Singapore's future and Minister Heng Swee Keat's Committee on the Future Economy will see to that, but we will need to be extraordinary in more ways than just our economy.

sections.label: Material capability and moral leadership
sections.summary: The passage cites the Gospel of Mark and says the new social compact must grow Singapore's material capability and moral leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Gospel of Mark says, "What good is it for someone to gain the whole world, yet forfeit their soul?" So, in our new social compact, we need to grow not just Singapore's material capability but also moral leadership.

sections.label: Functional parts of democracy
sections.summary: The passage says suggestions like smaller GRCs, racial representation in the Elected Presidency and electoral changes are functional parts of democracy, not its be all and end all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Page: 59 Moving forward, this will become more intense than in the past as society continues to mature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: There have been suggestions for smaller GRCs, racial representation in the Elected Presidency, further changes to the electoral system, but these are just functional parts of democracy, not the be all and end all of it.

sections.label: New social compact for all
sections.summary: The passage says the new social compact should include all Singaporeans but should not be left just to the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The new social compact should include all Singaporeans, but we should not just leave it to the Government.

sections.label: Jobs priority for Singaporeans
sections.summary: Slower growth creates an urgent need for job creation, and the speaker urges the Government to give Singaporeans priority for meaningful, well-paying jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: There have been many projections that there will be slower growth in the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, there is an urgent need to ensure that jobs continue to be created and Singaporeans will benefit from the creation of more jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to ensure that Singaporeans be given priority to secure jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Many Singaporeans also continue to be frustrated when they find that jobs which they aspire towards are taken and given to foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Hence, I urge the Government to ensure that our manpower policies are tweaked towards giving Singaporeans the best option to secure meaningful and well-paying jobs.

sections.label: Social assistance for retired Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to the Government to assess social assistance schemes based on income rather than home or asset type.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: What about Singaporeans who are retired, but living in private estates?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I appeal to the Government to assess our social assistance schemes based on income, rather than home or asset type.

sections.label: MediShield Life premium costs
sections.summary: The passage states that many worry about the cost of MediShield Life premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: While we have MediShield Life today, what many of us worry about is the cost of the premiums for MediShield Life.

sections.label: Elderly housing and family disputes
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned housing policies force elderly with unresolved family disputes to stay with their children, as they cannot rent flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Whilst I agree that ours should be a society where bonds of kinship run deep and people look out for one another, I am concerned that our housing policies inadvertently force our elderly to stay with their children even when they have unresolved disputes with one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, we do not allow our elderly to rent flats just because their children are able to provide for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This essentially means that the elderly parents or parents-in-law have no choice but to stay within the same household even though they are not on talking terms.

sections.label: MOE secondary school appeal policy
sections.summary: The speaker was surprised that MOE no longer entertains appeals for secondary school places if students did not meet PSLE cut-off points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Just last month, I was surprised to find out that MOE had implemented a policy – appeals for places in secondary schools will no longer be entertained if the students did not meet the school's PSLE cut-off points.

sections.label: Principal discretion versus PSLE score
sections.summary: The principal has discretion to decide appeals on merits, but the policy now seems to focus only on the PSLE score.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The principal, who is a very senior administrator, is given some discretion to decide whether to allow the appeal, depending on the merits of the appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, it seems that the policy now focuses only on the PSLE score.

sections.label: Falling exports and manufacturing contraction
sections.summary: Non-oil domestic exports fell 7.2% year-on-year in December, the PMI contracted six months, and 2015 port container volume was 8.7% lower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Recent data shows that on a year-on-year basis, our non-oil domestic exports fell 7.2% in December.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The December reading of the Singapore Purchasing Managers' Index which measures the economic health of the manufacturing sector has also shown six consecutive months of contraction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Annual container volume handled at our ports for 2015 was 8.7% lower compared to the year before.

sections.label: Foreign worker levy construction
sections.summary: In construction, the foreign worker levy for a basic skilled worker can be as high as S$950 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the construction industry, the foreign worker levy for a basic skilled worker can be as high as S$950 per month.

sections.label: Women and older worker participation
sections.summary: Women's labour force participation rose from 56.5% in 2010 to 60.4%, and those aged 55 to 64 rose from 61% to 69.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The labour force participation rate for women have increased from 56.5% in 2010 to 60.4% over the past five years, while the labour force participation rate of those aged 55 to 64 have increased even more from 61% to 69.5% over the past five years.

sections.label: Terrorism arrests and foreign fighters
sections.summary: Two Singaporean teenagers were arrested in October 2015, 27 radicalised Bangladeshis were repatriated, and over 25,000 fighters travelled to Iraq and Syria since 2011.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In October 2015, two Singaporean teenagers were arrested and detained for being involved in terrorism-related activities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: More recently, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) arrested and repatriated 27 radicalised Bangladeshis in Singapore who were planning to take part in extremist activities outside Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Since 2011, over 25,000 fighters from 100 different countries have travelled to Iraq and Syria, with rising numbers of Indonesians and Malaysians amongst them.

sections.label: Social media spreading radical ideologies
sections.summary: Social media lets radical ideologies invade thoughts without extremists entering a society, with about 46,000 Twitter accounts globally and at least 1,000 Facebook accounts in Southeast Asia supporting ISIS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We are now faced with a battle of ideologies, and the ubiquity of social media has allowed radical ideologies supporting terrorism to invade the thoughts of people without extremists having to physically enter a society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: There are some 46,000 Twitter accounts globally and at least 1,000 Facebook accounts in Southeast Asia supporting ISIS.

sections.label: Singapore joins counter-ISIS coalition
sections.summary: Singapore was the first Southeast Asian country to join the counter-ISIS coalition in November 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore was the first Southeast 	Page: 8 Asian country to join the counter-ISIS coalition in November 2014.

sections.label: Muslim leaders denounce terrorism
sections.summary: Muslim community and religious leaders have repeatedly denounced terrorist ideology and acts, including by ISIS, Al Qaeda and JI.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Indeed, each time a terror attack takes place, our Muslim community and religious leaders have repeatedly denounced the radical ideology articulated by terrorists and condemned the acts of these terrorist groups,including ISIS, Al Qaeda and Jemaah Islamiyah (JI).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, following the arrest and repatriation of the 27 radicalised Bangladeshis, Dr Mohamed Fatris Bakaram, Mufti of Singapore, publicly denounced extremism and extremist acts that threaten the security, peace and harmony of Singapore and the world.

sections.label: Ideological war and social media
sections.summary: The ideological war is fought in people's minds, made harder by social media, requiring religious understanding and social and psychological resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The ideological war confronting us is fought in the minds of our people, made more challenging with modern communication tools like social media.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We need to increase our religious understanding and also build up our social and psychological resilience to reduce our vulnerability towards those who exploit the Internet and social media with false teachings.

sections.label: Scholars address Christmas greeting ban
sections.summary: Religious and community leaders, including Habib Syed Hassan Al-Attas, spoke up, and the proposed ban on Christmas greetings has no Islamic basis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Many of us are heartened that, as reported in today's Berita Harian, senior and respected scholars, like Habib Syed Hassan Al-Attas, the Imam of Ba'alwie Mosque in Singapore, and other religious and community leaders have chosen to speak up and address this issue directly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We now know that the proposed ban on Christmas or other similar greetings has no Islamic basis.

sections.label: Greetings not against Islamic teachings
sections.summary: According to him, greeting a friend with "Gong Xi Fa Cai" or "Merry Christmas" is not against Islamic teachings or traditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: According to him, a Muslim greeting "Gong Xi Fa Cai" or "Merry Christmas" to a friend is not against Islamic teachings or traditions.

sections.label: Religiosity not the problem
sections.summary: Non-Muslims must be assured that religiosity is not the problem; misinterpretation and misrepresentation of religious beliefs and teachings is the source of terrorist thinking.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Non-Muslims need to know and they must be assured that religiosity per se is not the problem.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: It is the misinterpretation and misrepresentation of religious beliefs and teachings that is the source of terrorist thinking.

sections.label: Re-orientating religious leaders' world view
sections.summary: Religious and community leaders, including returning religious scholars, must be assisted to re-orientate their world view to be consistent with societal values.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Religious and community leaders, including returning religious scholars exposed to and potentially influenced by different societal structures, must be assisted to consciously re-orientate their world view to be consistent with our societal values and make-up – for our Muslim community, one that supports the tenet that Islam embraces and respects diversity – cultural, social, religious and political.

sections.label: Muslim leaders denounce radical ideology
sections.summary: Muslim religious leaders have denounced radical ideology, and Mufti Dr Fatris Bakaram publicly denounced extremism after 27 radicalised Bangladeshis were arrested and repatriated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Indeed, although our Muslim community in Singapore comes under the spotlight whenever a terror attack takes place, our Muslim religious leaders have irrevocably denounced strongly the radical ideology articulated violently by ISIS, Al-Qaeda or JI.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For instance, following the arrest and repatriation of the 27 radicalised Bangladeshis, our Mufti Dr Fatris Bakaram publicly denounced extremism and the extremist acts that threaten the security, peace and harmony in Singapore and in the world in general.

sections.label: Ideological war and social media
sections.summary: The effort is more critical now because an ideological war is fought in people's minds and is made more challenging by social media.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: However, this effort is even more critical now.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We are now faced with an ideological war that is fought in the minds of our people and it is made more challenging with modern communication tools like social media.

sections.label: Religious leaders voice views
sections.summary: Some might believe it is un-Islamic, but religious leaders like Imam Habib Syed Hasan Al Attas have voiced their views in Berita Harian.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Those who did not know better might be taken in and believe that it is, indeed, un-Islamic to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: However, in Singapore, fortunately, we have senior and respected religious leaders like Habib Syed Hasan Al Attas, who is the Imam from the Ba'alwi Mosque, and other religious and community leaders who have voiced their views, as published in today's Berita Harian.

sections.label: PERGAS president on greetings
sections.summary: Ustaz Hasbi Hassan, President of PERGAS, advises the Muslim community to be discerning and says wishing 'Gong Xi Fa Cai' or 'Merry Christmas' is not against Islamic teachings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Page: 12 Ustaz Hasbi Hassan, the President of PERGAS, agrees and advises that the Muslim community must be discerning in adapting to their circumstances and context.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: According to him, and I quote, "although there are different views about this issue, that is, wishing 'Gong Xi Fa Cai' or 'Merry Christmas', it is not against Islamic teachings or traditions".

sections.label: Religiosity not the problem
sections.summary: Non-Muslims must be assured that a community's religiosity is not a problem; misinterpretation and misrepresentation of religious beliefs become the source of terrorist thinking.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Non-Muslims need to know and they must be given the assurance that the religiosity of a community is not a problem.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: It is the misinterpretation and misrepresentation of religious beliefs and teachings that become the source of terrorist thinking.

sections.label: Social cohesion against radicalism
sections.summary: Without social cohesion and resilience, one terrorist attack could sow deep mistrust and create irreparable fault lines, so communities must stand together.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Without social cohesion and social resilience against the threat of radicalism, all it takes is one thing, just one terrorist attack, to sow deep mistrust and it may create irreparable fault lines in our society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Page: 13 (In English): Our security challenges are beyond traditional warfare.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We can overcome this ideological war and threats of terrorism by demonstrating social and psychological resilience and solidarity within the local Muslim community and with the rest of the non-Muslim community in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In the unfortunate event that an attack occurs, we must stand together as a united community to deal with the aftermath.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We should draw inspiration from brave societies like Australia when Australians showed solidarity by standing by their Muslim community in the wake of the Sydney hostage crisis, with many offering to ride with members of the Islamic faith to work on public transport.

sections.label: Responding to terrorist threats
sections.summary: Singapore must adapt to threats, prevent attacks, and when attacks happen, respond as a united community without succumbing to suspicion and fear.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We will and must continue to adapt to rise up to the threats of today and tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We must do all we can to prevent a terrorist attack here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: But when an attack happens, we must not succumb to our suspicions and fears.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We must fight back as a united community, respond effectively and recover well.

sections.label: Suspect's access to legal counsel
sections.summary: The Law Society President raised the issue of a suspect's right to access legal counsel before Police record the suspect's statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Recently, the President of the Law Society, Mr Thio Shen Yi, had, in his speech at the Opening of the Legal Year on 11 January 2016, brought up the issue of a suspect's right of access to legal counsel before the suspect's statement is recorded by the Police.

sections.label: Consulting lawyer before statements
sections.summary: The Law Society's Criminal Practice Committee recommended suspects consult a lawyer privately for up to one hour before Police record statements, which the speaker supports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Thio stated that the Law Society's Criminal Practice Committee has recommended that a suspect be allowed to consult a lawyer privately for up to one hour before statements are recorded by the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I agree with the President of the Law Society's call for the Government to accept this recommendation.

sections.label: Early disclosure of evidence
sections.summary: The Attorney-General made proposals for early disclosure of evidence in criminal cases by both the prosecution and defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The AG made proposals for early disclosure of evidence in criminal cases by both the prosecution and defence.

sections.label: Benefits of early disclosure
sections.summary: Disclosure, particularly early disclosure, of evidence promotes a transparent process and potentially reduces legal costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Disclosure and, particularly, early disclosure, of evidence promotes a transparent process and also potentially reduces legal costs.

sections.label: Raising legal aid income limits
sections.summary: The speaker believes the $10,000 disposable income limit is too restrictive and a moderate increase could help more low-income Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Many people need lawyers to assist them beyond giving advice for 20 minutes in the manner that we see at community legal clinics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I believe the current limits of $10,000 disposable income is still too restrictive and a moderate increase on the limits may provide much needed assistance to many more low-income earning Singaporeans who are caught by the current limits.

sections.label: Civil Service independence and neutrality
sections.summary: The independence and political neutrality of the Civil Service and Statutory Boards must be fiercely maintained for Singaporeans' confidence in their non-partisan nature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The independence and political neutrality of the Civil Service and Statutory Boards must be fiercely maintained so that Singaporeans will always have complete confidence in the non-partisan nature of these institutions.

sections.label: Freedom of Information Act and ombudsman
sections.summary: The speaker echoes a call for a Freedom of Information Act and says the Government should consider an independent office of ombudsman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For this reason, I would echo the previous call for the introduction of a Freedom of Information Act by my colleague Mr Pritam Singh who spoke about this in his speech at the President's Address in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government should consider setting up an independent office of ombudsman.

sections.label: Affordable legal fees for judicial review
sections.summary: The average Singaporean must be able to afford reasonable legal fees to commence a judicial review application, or legal rights are merely academic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The average Singaporean must also be able to afford reasonable legal fees to commence the judicial review application, or the rights under the law will be merely academic.

sections.label: Unsustainable borrowings and Global Financial Crisis
sections.summary: Unsustainable borrowings fuelled excessive consumption for decades, but after the Global Financial Crisis this unsustainable borrowing stopped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For the last few decades, we have had unsustainable borrowings that have fuelled 	Page: 17 excessive consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But after the Global Financial Crisis (GFC), this unsustainable borrowing has stopped.

sections.label: Jobs lost to technology, export economy
sections.summary: A report said 15 major economies will lose around seven million jobs to technology in five years, and Singapore's export-based economy is under siege.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A recent World Economic Foreign Report said that the 15 major economies in the world in the next five years will lose around seven million jobs to technology; seven million jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The underlying theme is actually that our mainstream export-based economy that has fuelled Singapore's success for the last few decades is now under siege from excessive competition and from disruptive technology and business models.

sections.label: World-class funding environment for startups
sections.summary: A world-class funding environment must be built, as a pressing gap exists in seed, Series A and mezzanine funding despite a good venture capitalist base.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Two, we have to build a world-class funding environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We already have a good base of venture capitalists today, but, because of the recent uptick in number of startups and a lack of high-profile market exits, there is a pressing gap in seed, Series A, mezzanine funding.

sections.label: Barclay's President on finance jobs
sections.summary: Barclay's President said 20% to 50% of finance jobs will be replaced by technology in the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Barclay's President recently said that in the next 10 years, 20% to 50% of finance jobs will be replaced by technology; 20% to 50% in just 10 years.

sections.label: Regulatory sandboxes and double-envelope tenders
sections.summary: Agencies can create regulatory sandboxes and use a double-envelope tender to look beyond established firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, we can create regulatory sandboxes to test out new ideas on a small scale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)

sections.label: CLAS lawyers helped poor accused
sections.summary: Mr Thio Shen Yi said CLAS lawyers helped 1,300 poor people accused of crime in 2015, a 300% increase from 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In contrast, I note that Mr Thio Shen Yi, Senior Counsel, the President of the Law Society, mentioned at the Opening of the Legal Year in 2016 that last year, that is, in 2015, the CLAS lawyers helped 1,300 poor people accused of crime, an increase of 300% from 2014.

sections.label: Constitutional right to legal counsel
sections.summary: Article 9(3) of the Constitution sets out an arrested person's right to counsel, which Courts say is exercised within a reasonable time after arrest.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Moving on to another point that Mr Dennis Tan raised, which is access to counsel, the rights of an accused person to legal counsel are set out in Article 9(3) of our Constitution, which states "where a person is arrested, he shall be informed as soon as may be of the grounds of his arrest and shall be allowed to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of his choice".

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our Courts, in interpreting the Constitution, have determined that this right to legal counsel is to be exercised within a reasonable time after arrest and not immediately after arrest.

sections.label: Third-party communication and investigations
sections.summary: Letting an accused communicate with third parties before Police finish investigations may compromise investigations, especially where testimony leads to crime scenes and accomplices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Permitting an accused person to communicate with third parties before the Police can wrap up their investigations may compromise the investigations, especially so in cases where the Prosecution relies primarily on the testimony of witnesses and accused persons to lead them to the crime scenes, accomplices and other corroborative evidence.

sections.label: Criminal discovery and access to justice
sections.summary: Criminal discovery provisions exist and Courts set out these obligations; the Ministry of Law will work with other Ministries to balance individual rights with society's needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On criminal discovery, there are provisions in place for criminal discovery and our Courts have set out what these obligations entail.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance and Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In essence, the Ministry of Law remains committed to the promotion of access to justice and we will work with the other Ministries, including MHA, to ensure that we have the right kind of 	Page: 67 system that takes into account the rights of the individuals and yet balances that with the needs of society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Social well-being for our people can only be enhanced and sustained if we have a growing economy that generates the financial resources to pay for the needed expenditures, which include security which the House talked about last two days, as well as to provide good job opportunities for our citizen workforce.

sections.label: Singapore's past growth competitive advantages
sections.summary: Singapore created competitive advantages through infrastructure, connectivity, FTAs, MNCs, pro-business policies and low taxes, but capacity constraints mean lower growth and price competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Not just because we do it cheaper than others but rather, we were able to create our own competitive advantages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We engineered strong growth in manufacturing and services by way of a whole-of-Government approach – building the necessary infrastructure ahead of demand – ports, airport, industrial spaces – continually developing international linkages and connectivity to facilitate trade and investments, free trade agreements (FTAs), multinational corporations (MNCs) with their international links, instituting pro-business policies, among others, our low tax regime, and ensuring that there are sufficient manpower resources for businesses, both local sourced and foreign sourced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Continuing this way of growing our economy is still a viable option, particularly in areas of high value adding, and it remains a policy option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, given the inherent constraints in our capacity, that would mean we have to settle for a much lower growth range going forward and are destined to always compete with the next cheaper player.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We will also be at the mercy of the volatile global demand cycles, which tends to impact us more as a small and open economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, just adding value and competing on prices has become less of a value proposition for us, especially so as our economy matures and that we are near the limits in terms of manpower growth and land spaces.

sections.label: Start-up scene innovation output
sections.summary: Singapore ranks high in innovation inputs but innovation output has not been as encouraging, mostly in wholesale trade and financial services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These are necessary conditions for a vibrant start-up scene.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, while Singapore ranks high in world rankings in terms innovation inputs, such as infrastructural support and business sophistication, the innovation output has not been as encouraging; and it is mostly in the area of wholesale trade and financial services.

sections.label: Education, skills and innovation
sections.summary: The speaker says innovation rests on education, skills and individuals' passion and risk attitudes, and echoes calls for MOE to reduce stress in the education system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Successful innovation rests on the foundation of education, skills and, more importantly, the passion and risk attitudes of individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I echo calls by many Members in this House for the Ministry of Education (MOE) to do more to diffuse the high stress and high stakes situation of our education system, from the primary school to tertiary level.

sections.label: Education beyond exam performance
sections.summary: The speaker states that Singapore's education system cannot be narrowly focused on examination-based academic performance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Our education system cannot be narrowly focused on examination-based academic performance.

sections.label: Arts, sports and CCA weightage
sections.summary: The speaker says schools should not crowd out arts, sports and aesthetic subjects, wants their weightage increased, and was disturbed that some schools stopped CCAs in PSLE or O-Level years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, we need to distinguish the truth from the facts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Also, schools should avoid crowding out less easily assessed curriculum such arts, sports and aesthetic subjects as these activities stimulate a wide range of social, thinking and behavioural skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Rather, the weightage of these subjects should be increased so that learning in school can be fun and can be enriching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, when I heard that in some schools, co-curricular activities (CCA) were stopped for students in the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) year or the "O" Level year, just so that the students can focus on their major examinations, it disturbed me quite a fair bit.

sections.label: MOE reducing academic emphasis
sections.summary: The speaker urges keeping students in the system to learn, and is glad MOE Ministers reiterated reducing over-emphasis on academic results and making learning more enjoyable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Keep them in the system so that they can learn on and gain knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am glad that the two Ministers at MOE have reiterated in their Ministry's Addendum that MOE will reduce the over-emphasis on academic results and make learning more enjoyable.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and employability concerns
sections.summary: The speaker cites a US study that 47% of US employment is at risk of computerisation, praises SkillsFuture's $500 credit and ownership of learning, but questions whether its courses have sufficient depth and improve employability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A recent study in the United States (US) estimated that 47% of the total US employment is at risk of being computerised or digitised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture could be the mindset game changer and especially with the SkillsFuture's credit of $500 that will certainly help ease the costs barriers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What I like about SkillsFuture is that it enables individuals to take ownership of their own learning journey and hopefully inculcate the attitude to always seek new knowledge and to improve skills as part of their lifestyle routine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, we should also be mindful about whether the training and courses under SkillsFuture would have sufficient depth and focus and whether it would help improve individual employability and skills mastery.

sections.label: Updating laws for entrepreneurs
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore's laws, rules and Government Instruction Manuals were written some time ago and may need updating for a more entrepreneurial society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Our laws, our rules as well as our Instruction Manuals (IMs) in the Government are written quite some time ago and may need to be updated to cater for a more entrepreneurial society.

sections.label: Managing foreign manpower supply
sections.summary: Foreign manpower supply should be managed and calibrated according to physical and social constraints, as international centres like New York and London have done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By all means, manage and calibrate our overall foreign manpower supply in accordance to our physical and social constraints like what many international centres, such as New York and London, have done.

sections.label: ASEAN terrorist attacks
sections.summary: Terrorist attacks in Bangkok in 2015 and Jakarta a fortnight ago show ISIS has brought its terror to the region's doorstep.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The ASEAN region has taken a dangerous turn with the terrorist attacks in Bangkok in 2015 and in Jakarta a fortnight ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: ISIS has successfully taken its terror and fight right to our doorstep.

sections.label: Countering radical ideologies online
sections.summary: A terrorist attack in Singapore is no longer remote, and the speaker hopes the Government will counter radical ideologies online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: A terrorist attack in Singapore is no longer a remote possibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: While it is reassuring that the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) will strengthen our border security and tap into technology to help fight criminals and terrorist threats, it is my hope that this Government will also put effort in countering the spread of radical ideologies online.

sections.label: Study into tuition culture
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOE to commission a study into the tuition culture to help educators formulate better policy decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Or has it merely shifted more of the learning from the classroom to the private tutors?

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I am sure MOE would like to know the effectiveness of the "Teach Less, Learn More" model, but without a corresponding study into the tuition culture here, nothing can be conclusive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I do urge MOE to commission a study into the tuition culture because it will help our educators to formulate better policy decisions in the next chapter.

sections.label: Foreign talents as role models
sections.summary: The Government pursued an Olympic medal using foreign talents hoping they could be role models for young athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: We need role models in life to inspire ourselves to greater heights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: This Government has gone to great lengths to pursue an Olympic medal using foreign talents in the hope that the move will bring glory to the nation and the imported Olympians could be role models for our young athletes.

sections.label: Students' Boeing patent
sections.summary: Six Singapore polytechnic students had their invention patented by Boeing and were listed as co-inventors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The benefits that such deep collaboration brings to the schools, the students and the community at large are immeasurable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I am heartened to read in the papers that six students from Singapore polytechnics have had their invention patented by Boeing and their names listed as co-inventors of the patent recently.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and education outcomes
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture initiative is called a step in the right direction, and getting education right is said to get security, economy, society, living environment and nation building right.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture initiative announced last year is certainly a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Each successive cohort that leaves our classroom must be resilient and, most important of all, must have a sense of belonging, without which we can never have an exceptional nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: I certainly believe that when we get our education right, we will get our security right, we will get our economy right, we will also get our society right, we will get our living environment right and most important of all, we will get our nation building right.

sections.label: Machines replacing replicable job tasks
sections.summary: Every job task that can be replicated can be replaced by a machine, and income gaps widen between those whose skills are in demand and those who cannot catch up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Every job task that can be replicated can be replaced by a machine.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Income gaps widen between those whose skills are in demand and those who cannot catch up.

sections.label: Three unhealthy P's in education
sections.summary: A GPC member for Education of 10 years says the education system is pimpled by three unhealthy P's: preoccupation with academic scores, parentocracy, and physical segregation of students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As a GPC member for Education for the last 10 years, I have met many authentic, diligent and professional educators who want the best for our young.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, Madam, our education system is one that is pimpled by three unhealthy "P"s: one, a pre-occupation with academic scores; two, parentocracy; and three, physical segregation of our students.

sections.label: Impairments from exams and tuition
sections.summary: It is called an impairment when popular school posting uses cut-off points of high-stake examinations at age 12, and when teachers teach to test and parents feed the $1-billion tuition industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is an impairment when the posting criteria to popular schools is based on cut-off points of high-stake examinations at the age of 12.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is an impairment when teachers teach to test, and parents feed the $1-bilion tuition industry in order to ace examinations and increase one's options.

sections.label: Direct School Admissions and affluence
sections.summary: In the Direct School Admissions programme, it is an open secret that children from more affluent backgrounds stand a higher chance of benefitting since they could be nurtured from young in arts or sports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In the case of the Direct School Admissions (DSA) programme, for example, it is an open secret that children from more affluent backgrounds stand a higher chance of benefitting from it since they could be nurtured from young in the arts or even sports.

sections.label: Removing PSLE and through-train model
sections.summary: Suggestion two is to remove the Primary School Leaving Examination without compromising academic rigour and pilot a 10-year through-train school model.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Suggestion two is to remove the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) without compromising academic rigour and pilot a 10-year through-train school model.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Seriously, walk another path − remove one high-stake examination, the PSLE!

sections.label: Ending physical segregation in learning
sections.summary: Suggestion three calls for re-dreaming and ending the practice of physically segregating people who learn differently.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Suggestion three is to re-dream and slay the sacred cow of physically segregating people who learn differently.

sections.label: Piloting inclusive education villages
sections.summary: Suggestion four proposes piloting inclusive education villages across Singapore housing students of different abilities and backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Suggestion four is to pilot inclusive education villages across Singapore to house students of different abilities and backgrounds.

sections.label: Government moral authority for adoption
sections.summary: It asks whether the Government can use moral authority to commit schools and corporations to regularly adopt vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Can the Government exercise the moral authority to commit schools and corporations, including Government agencies to adopt, on a regular and longer-term basis, vulnerable groups, especially the low-skilled elderly and those with special needs and/or disabilities?

sections.label: Citizen engagement and collaboration
sections.summary: It states citizen engagement and agencies like CDCs aim to help the vulnerable through collaboration rather than shaming.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: That is the purpose of the next series of citizen engagement in the form of the SG50 discussions, and the mission of agencies such as the Community Development Councils (CDCs).

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There is still much more to be done for the vulnerable in our midst, but they will not get any better unless we collaborate with, instead of simply naming and shaming or pushing away, those who could make a difference with us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The "Future of Us" is only as strong as our willingness to be part of the solution and dirty our hands if we need to, and our ability to genuinely collaborate – giving credit when credit is due; refraining from naming, shaming and posturing to score points for oneself or for one's political party.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Someone once said in a political satire that politicians will lose votes when they advocate something controversial, but they will lose an election if they choose to be too bold or courageous.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But for the deep holes that confront our nation, I urge us all to be bold and walk another path if need be; for not doing so, may not only cost us an election but cost us our beloved country.

sections.label: Action Plan for Successful Ageing
sections.summary: It describes the Action Plan for Successful Ageing, its consultations, initiatives, and co-located Senior Care Centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We need to plan far ahead to adequately meet this challenge.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Hence, the Ministerial Committee on Ageing announced last year an Action Plan for Successful Ageing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: It is a collaborative effort among Government agencies, Voluntary Welfare and Non-profit organisations, business and community organisations as well as union leaders, and reflects the aspirations and ideas of more than 4,000 Singaporeans from all walks of life who were widely consulted over a period of close to one year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Action Plan offers more than 60 initiatives in 12 areas such as health and wellness, employment, volunteerism and retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) has plans to co-locate Senior Care Centres (SCCs) at Community Clubs and town hubs such as at the Bedok Integrated Complex.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The first such SCC, co-located with Ci Yuan Community Club, will be welcoming its first clients in the coming months.

sections.label: Abuse and neglect of elderly
sections.summary: It notes painful minority cases of cheating, abuse or neglect of elderly parents, including financial abuse by children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Though still a minority, it is painful to read about cases of cheating, abuse or even neglect of elderly parents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: It was recently reported that social workers are seeing more senior citizens who have been cheated or financially abused by their children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In one tragic case, an elderly parent was convinced to sell her home to live with her son who purchased another house with her money, only to be asked to find a home of her own when the relationship with the son's family turned sour.

sections.label: Mature workers revenue per salary
sections.summary: The company has seen mature workers bring in more revenue per dollar of salary than some younger staff.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As a result, it has seen mature workers in the company bring in more revenue per dollar of salary than some of the younger staff.

sections.label: TAFEP on workplace ageism complaints
sections.summary: TAFEP says ageism complaints are falling but noted some employers still lack urgency in employing older workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: According to the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP), complaints against workplace ageism have been falling, but TAFEP also noted at a seminar last year that some employers here still lack a sense of urgency when it comes to employing older workers.

sections.label: Goodlife Makan community kitchen
sections.summary: Goodlife! started a community kitchen called Goodlife Makan after noticing many stay-alone elderly in Marine Terrace.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In Marine Parade, the local senior activity centre Goodlife! started a community kitchen in the precinct called "Goodlife Makan", after they noticed that there were many stay-alone elderly in Marine Terrace.

sections.label: NCMP scheme nine Opposition members
sections.summary: The NCMP scheme presently allows nine highest scoring Opposition members to enter Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The NCMP scheme presently allows for nine highest scoring Opposition members to enter Parliament.

sections.label: Support expanding NCMP scheme
sections.summary: The speaker supports expanding the NCMP scheme to 12 or beyond, citing diversity and value of varied perspectives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In fact, I believe that with greater diversity of our population, as well as rising political interest and awareness among a better educated population, such a desire would grow.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: I would thus support further expansion of the NCMP scheme, say to 12 or even beyond, recognising the value of having issues dissected from various perspectives that can sharpen and refine policy formulation.

sections.label: Parliamentary seats increased since 2011
sections.summary: Parliamentary seats rose from 87 in 2011 to 89 in 2015 and could continue rising with population growth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The number of Parliamentary seats has also increased since the last election in 2011 from 87 to 89 in 2015, and it is envisaged that this number could continue to rise given the rising population.

sections.label: Elected Presidency and candidate capital
sections.summary: An IPS survey after the 2011 Presidential Elections suggests most Singaporeans want to elect the President, and a candidate's company minimum paid up capital should be raised from $100 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Some commentators have suggested that we do away with elections for the Presidency by the People.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: However, an Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) survey after the 2011 Presidential Elections suggests that a majority of Singaporeans wish to choose their President through an election.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: For instance, the minimum paid up capital of the private or public company that a candidate leads as CEO or chairman of the board of directors should be raised significantly from the current $100 million.

sections.label: Ageing population and support ratio
sections.summary: In 2013 the number crossed 10%, would reach 24% by 2030, and the old age support ratio would drop from 1:5.2 to 1:2.3 in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2013, that number had crossed the 10% mark, and by 2030, this would increase to 24%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our old age support ratio would drop from today's 1:5.2 to 1:2.3 in 2030.

sections.label: Elderly wellness programmes in constituencies
sections.summary: Wellness programmes for elderly residents exist in all 87 constituencies in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am very happy to see the many efforts in our community for our elderly to keep healthy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There are wellness programmes in all 87 constituencies in Singapore.

sections.label: Driver health screening programmes
sections.summary: About 3,000 taxi drivers had health screening and follow-up consultations, and since last June about 400 bus drivers went through a customised programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, some 3,000 taxi drivers have had health screening and follow-up consultations and since last June, about 400 bus drivers had gone through a customised programme that includes chronic disease management, eyesight monitoring, ergonomics and hydration.

sections.label: Seniors prefer ageing in place
sections.summary: An MSF survey found about 80% of household heads aged 65 or above prefer to age-in-place at their existing flats.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In a recent survey by the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), about 80% of household heads aged 65 or above prefer to age-in-place at their existing flats.

sections.label: Increase in care places
sections.summary: Since 2011 nursing home beds rose by 1,000, home care places by 2,700 and centre-based care by 1,000, with Government targets for 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Since 2011, nursing homes beds has increased by 1,000, home care places by 2,700 and centre-based care by another 1,000 places.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am glad to note that the Government is committed to increasing nursing home beds to 17,000, home care places to 10,000 and centre-based care to 6,200 places, by the year 2020.

sections.label: Elderly healthcare subsidies and schemes
sections.summary: Patients can receive subsidies up to 100%, eligibility broadened from half to two-thirds of households by 2012, alongside other elderly schemes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Patients can receive subsidies of up to 100% in some cases, and that eligibility has broadened from half to two-thirds of households by the year 2012.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Other measures include the Enhanced Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly, the Senior Mobility and Enabling Fund, ElderShield and the Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme.

sections.label: Subsidised nursing home rooms
sections.summary: Medical colleagues called on MOH to reconsider building subsidised single and twin rooms, citing research on dementia residents' anxiety, irritability, aggression and sleep.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: My medical colleagues have recently called upon the MOH to reconsider building subsidised single and twin rooms in nursing homes, as research has shown that residents with dementia in nursing homes with individual rooms have less anxiety, irritability and aggression, and also sleep better.

sections.label: Long-term care financing and elderly support
sections.summary: It proposes a bigger insurance role in long-term care, a comprehensive ElderShield review, more funding for health and mobility aids research, and foreign partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Third, we can consider a bigger role for insurance in long-term care financing, just as we enhanced MediShield.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As there are plans to review ElderShield, I urge MOH to be comprehensive in this exercise and address the most important elements – the role of individuals in saving, the role of the family in supporting them and the role of the community and Government in sharing of the risks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Lastly, in line with our aim to be a Smart Nation, I hope that the Government will increase funding for the research and development of health and mobility aids and monitoring devices such as variables and robotics and even drones to help out our elderly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To accelerate our development in this area, we should look into partnering foreign leading firms and institutions in this industry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Much has been said about the future of us but literally, the future of us is ourselves in old age.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And to answer this call, I would ask that we, all of us, work together to help our senior citizens remain healthy and socially connected within the community, to give them and their family better assurances in their golden years and provide options for them to age within the community.

sections.label: Good policies and good politics
sections.summary: Beyond individual policies, the President said at the end of his speech that good policies and good politics are both needed.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: One fundamental requirement, beyond individual policies, was what the President said at the end of his speech – we need good policies, but we also need good politics.

sections.label: Government term and good politics
sections.summary: The Government will do this in its term, but good policies require good politics because the two go hand-in-hand.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And this is what my Government will do in this term.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But in order to have these good policies done, we also must have good politics, because the two go hand-in-hand.

sections.label: Responsibility for political institutions
sections.summary: It is not an urgent task for today, but this generation must ensure political institutions and system keep working well for future generations.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: It is not an urgent task that you must do today instead of tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But it is this generation's responsibility to make sure that our political institutions and system continue to work well, well beyond the term of this team, and work well for future generations.

sections.label: Countries facing division and gridlock
sections.summary: Some countries face division and gridlock, with paralysed government, like the US.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But if we look around the world, in fact, it is not such a simple matter.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: There are some countries which face division and gridlock, and the government is paralysed, like the US.

sections.label: US Federal Government shutdown 2013
sections.summary: In 2013, the Federal Government shut down for 16 days because Congress could not pass a Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Three years ago in 2013, the Federal Government had to shut down for 16 days because Republicans and Democrats in Congress could not agree to pass a Budget.

sections.label: No perfect model worldwide
sections.summary: There is no perfect model anywhere, much less one to import wholesale and apply in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The moral of the story is there is no perfect model anywhere in the world, much less one in which we can import wholesale and apply in Singapore.

sections.label: High-quality government requirements
sections.summary: It must enable a high-quality government that is accountable, honest, competent, and effective.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: First, it must enable us to have a high-quality government – accountable, honest, competent, and effective.

sections.label: First-class government in Singapore
sections.summary: Without a first-class government led by exceptional leaders, Singapore would not exist today.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: It is something which we have, which we can do, which others can see; not so easy for others to duplicate.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: I will put this quite bluntly; if we had not had a first-class government in Singapore, led by exceptional leaders who are able to foresee problems, head them off, seize opportunities, reap dividends for Singapore and mobilise people to work with them and to support policies – sometimes tough ones – we would not have Singapore today.

sections.label: Election spending comparison
sections.summary: Parties spent $7 million in General Elections, less than $3 per voter, versus US$7 billion in 2012.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: All of the parties together, added up, during the national General Elections, they spent all of $7 million, less than $3 per voter.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: In 2012, when they last had their Presidential election together with Congressional elections, it cost them US$7 billion.

sections.label: Parliament as serious forum
sections.summary: Parliament must be a serious forum where big issues like defence, economy, tax and spending, and future plans are discussed and decided.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Parliament here must be a serious forum where big issues are discussed and decided – defence, economy, choices to tax and spend, and plans for the future.

sections.label: Political system upholds multiracial society
sections.summary: The political system must uphold a multiracial society.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Fourthly, our political system must uphold a multiracial society.

sections.label: Encourage multiracial and secular politics
sections.summary: Splitting along fault lines would end us, so the political system must encourage multiracial and secular politics, not racial or religious politics.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: If we ever split along one of these fault lines, that would be the end of us.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Therefore, our political system must encourage multiracial and secular politics, not racial or religious politics.

sections.label: Stabilisers protecting reserves and public service
sections.summary: Stabilisers are needed to protect reserves and safeguard public service integrity, since one government could spend decades of reserves and turn elections into auctions.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: It is a small personality, same title, but is quite a different entity indeed.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We may be small but we still need stabilisers, and we especially need stabilisers in two areas: (a) protecting our reserves and (b) safeguarding the integrity of the public service.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Because these are two critical elements that give us safety, security, assurance and resources for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: It has taken us decades to build up our foreign Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: If we do not have a second key, and you happen to have a generous or profligate government, then one government can spend it all and bring you back to zero.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Elections will become auctions, where the parties compete to be more generous than the other, offering what it can do to voters by raiding the bank.

sections.label: Second key for stabilising government
sections.summary: A second key is needed to prevent this, and the challenge is ensuring it strengthens and stabilises the system of Government.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: To prevent this, or at least to make this harder, this system needs a second key.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The challenge for us is how to ensure this second key strengthens and stabilises our system of Government.

sections.label: Rejecting FCO drafts, NCMP scheme
sections.summary: He did not take in the FCO experts' drafts because they had not understood the context, and explained this in 1984 when moving amendments to create the NCMP scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: He did not take in the brand-new versions drafted by the British experts in the Foreign and Commonwealth Office (FCO) because he concluded that the experts had not understood the context, nor why we had made certain basic decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: He explained this to the House in 1984, when he moved the Constitutional Amendments to create the Non-Constituency Member of Parliament (NCMP) scheme.

sections.label: New institutions in Parliament
sections.summary: Singapore kept its seating system but introduced NCMPs, NMPs, GRCs and an Elected President.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We do not sit in a semi-circle, the way the Americans sit in a semi-circle, or the way the European legislatures sit in a semi-circle.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: We kept that system but subsequently, we introduced new institutions – Non-Constituency Members of Parliament, Nominated Members of Parliament, Group Representation Constituencies (GRCs) and the institution of an Elected President.

sections.label: Barisan Sosialis walkout 1965
sections.summary: After Independence and Separation, the Barisan Sosialis Opposition walked out of Parliament in 1965.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: After Independence, after Separation, the Barisan Sosialis Opposition walked out of Parliament in 1965.

sections.label: Government rule until 1981
sections.summary: This let the Government govern decisively from 1965 until 1981, when J B Jeyaretnam was elected.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: This enabled the Government to govern decisively and effectively in the vital first years of our nationhood.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: It lasted from 1965 until 1981 when the first Opposition Member, J B Jeyaretnam, was elected to Parliament.

sections.label: Opposition voices found useful
sections.summary: They concluded it was good for the Government and Singapore system to have Opposition voices in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: After some time, they concluded, to their surprise, that despite all the to-ing and fro-ing and unpleasantness, it was good for the Government and good for the Singapore system that we have Opposition voices in Parliament because the Opposition could express opposing views, could question and criticise the Government and could make Ministers justify their actions.

sections.label: NCMP scheme proposed 1984
sections.summary: Mr Lee proposed the NCMP scheme in 1984, ensuring a minimum number of Opposition Members, now nine.
