sections.summary: The passage says this may be the tip of the iceberg and urges employers who retrench to let go of Singaporean PMEs last.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: This may well be just the tip of the iceberg.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We need to brace ourselves and, when employers do downsize and retrench, we urge them to let go of our Singaporean PMEs last.

sections.label: CSP subsidies for mature PMEs
sections.summary: The CSP provides subsidies to employers who hire mature PMEs aged 40 and above for jobs paying $4,000 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The CSP provides subsidies to employers who hire mature PMEs 40 years and above for jobs paying $4,000 and Page: 61 above.

sections.label: Sustaining and expanding CSP
sections.summary: The passage says the CSP can sustain a PME as long as the job is done well and suggests promoting and expanding it to all PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: And if you ask how long it can sustain the PME, I would say it is for as long as you do your job and do it well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I suggest we should further promote, position and expand the CSP to provide targeted help to all PMEs.

sections.label: Retooling workers for uncertain economy
sections.summary: The passage states workers must re-calibrate and re-set mental models, employers must re-innovate and restructure, and collective efforts must triple.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: As we move into an increasingly unstable, unpredictable and uncertain economic landscape, our workers need to re-calibrate ourselves and re-set our mental models.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Employers and businesses must not be content with just re-adjusting but need to re-innovate and restructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We need to triple our collective efforts to retool ourselves to be ready, relevant and resilient.

sections.label: Multiracial diversity in political system
sections.summary: The Prime Minister highlighted upholding multiracial diversity, including equal opportunities for minorities in the Elected Presidency and GRC system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister yesterday highlighted the importance of upholding multiracial diversity in our political system; in particular for minorities to have equal opportunities for political representation in the Elected Presidency as well as the GRC system.

sections.label: Smaller GRCs and constituent connection
sections.summary: The passage states smaller GRCs as proposed by the Prime Minister will let Members of Parliament connect more closely with constituents and represent them better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Smaller GRCs – as proposed by the Prime Minister – will enable us as Members Parliament to connect more closely with our constituents and represent them even better.

sections.label: Training and educational opportunities
sections.summary: Training and educational opportunities such as SkillsFuture and MENDAKI's Future Ready Committee aim to level the playing field for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: There have been many useful training and educational opportunities to help to level the playing field for all Singaporeans, no matter what their starting point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These include the SkillsFuture and the recently set up Future Ready Committee in MENDAKI, amongst others.

sections.label: Young community median age
sections.summary: The community's median age is 31.4, compared to the national median age of 37.4, and now is a good time to build a better future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If there is a good time in our community's history where we can all rise and build a better future together, that time is now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We have many young people with a median age of 31.4, compared to the national median age of 37.4.

sections.label: MENDAKI Sense jobseekers qualifications
sections.summary: In 2015, 40% of people seeking employment through MENDAKI Sense had N or O level certificates as their highest qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If we look at the job market now, 40% of people who seek employment through "MENDAKI Sense" in 2015, for instance, are those who have "N" or "O" level certificates as their highest qualifications.

sections.label: Discrimination complaints and enquiries
sections.summary: TAFEP's 2014 annual report shows complaints against discriminatory practices almost halved from 2013, while enquiries rose about twice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Thankfully, those days are firmly in our past.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am particularly pleased to note that, based on the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP)'s 2014 annual report, the number of complaints lodged against discriminatory practices in 2014 had been almost halved from 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The number of enquiries in this regard has risen by about twice from the year before.

sections.label: Fines for unlawful discrimination
sections.summary: Employers guilty of unlawful discrimination could be fined up to A$54,000 per contravention for a corporation and A$10,800 for an individual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Employers guilty of unlawful discrimination could be fined up to A$54,000 per contravention for a corporation and A$10,800 per contravention for an individual.

sections.label: Employment Claims Tribunal for PMETs
sections.summary: MOM is introducing the Employment Claims Tribunal, which covers PMETs earning above $4,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: MOM is introducing the Employment Claims Tribunal which covers PMETs earning above $4,500.

sections.label: Sanctions on errant employers
sections.summary: The passage states that ensuring equal employment opportunities requires power to impose meaningful sanctions on errant employers, as in Australia and Finland.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If we, as a nation, are serious about ensuring that all Singaporeans have equal employment opportunities, we must also have the power to impose meaningful sanctions upon errant employers, as the laws in Australia and Finland allow.

sections.label: PMET layoffs and e2i applicants
sections.summary: The passage reports lowest employment growth in six years, most laid-off employees being PMETs, and e2i PMET applicants rising from 128 to 337.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, employment growth in Singapore in the first three quarters of 2015 was the lowest in six years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The hon Member Patrick Tay has highlighted some of that earlier, but the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) reported in the first three quarters of 2015, a significant majority of seven in 10 of employees laid-off from their jobs were PMETs, many of them degree-holders aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Between 2014 and 2015, the Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) experienced a more than doubling of the number of PMETs approaching the organisation for assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: From 128 applicants in 2014, e2i saw 337 applicants registering their interest to undergo intervention programme last year.

sections.label: SMEs in Singapore
sections.summary: The passage states SMEs make up 99% of companies, employ 70% of the workforce and contribute nearly 50% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: SMEs make up 99% of the companies in Singapore, employ 70% of the workforce and contribute to nearly 50% of our GDP.

sections.label: Elected Presidency and NCMP numbers
sections.summary: The passage states the Elected Presidency safeguards against loose fiscal policy and notes NCMP numbers rose from six to nine, with a wish to raise it to 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The institution of the Elected Presidency is a key safeguard against loose fiscal policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I agree that we need to review it to make it a stronger safeguard, as said by the Prime Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Since it started in 1984, with an upper limit of six NCMPs, this was increased to nine in 2010 and Prime Minister Lee said that he would like to raise the number to 12.

sections.label: Special education and Open Door Programme
sections.summary: The passage states special education spending rose 50% over five years and the Open Door Programme has encouraged employers to hire PWDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The spending on special education has increased 50% over the last five years and the Open Door Programme, launched in 2007, has gone some way in encouraging employers to hire PWDs.

sections.label: Disabled employment survey findings
sections.summary: The passage states there are no local employment statistics for the disabled, and a 2014 survey of 100 companies found 20% open to hiring PWDs but only 7% did.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: There are no statistics on the local employment rate amongst the disabled in Singapore, who are defined as those with physical, sensory, intellectual and developmental impairments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, a strategic market research consultancy, Spire Research and Consulting, conducted a survey of 100 companies in January 2014 which showed that while 20% were open to hiring PWDs, only 7% actually did so.

sections.label: Bus 51 versus train travel
sections.summary: Bus service 51 from Hougang to Jurong East covers close to 38 kilometres and takes about two hours and 42 minutes, while a train ride takes 53 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For example, bus service 51 plies from Hougang Bus Interchange to Jurong East Interchange, covering close to 38 kilometres and the average traveling time is about two hours and 42 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In contrast, a train ride from Hougang to Jurong East takes only 53 minutes, that is, a saving of almost two hours.

sections.label: Eliminating long bus services
sections.summary: Eliminating 14 bus services with routes longer than 30 kilometres could free resources to run 40 new feeder bus services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If we are able to eliminate 14 bus services with bus routes longer than 30 kilometres, we could easily use the same resources to run 40 new feeder bus services.

sections.label: Regulators and sharing economy revenue
sections.summary: Regulators worldwide do not quite know how to deal with this phenomenon, estimated to generate US$335 billion in revenue worldwide by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Regulators worldwide do not quite know how to deal with this phenomenon, which is estimated to generate US$335 billion in revenue worldwide by 2025.

sections.label: Short-term stay rental rules
sections.summary: In Singapore, private homes can only be rented out for six months or more, and HDB flat owners cannot sublet units or rooms to tourists for short-term stays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Page: 70 In Singapore, private homes can only be rented out for six months or more, while HDB flat owners are not allowed to sublet their units or rooms to tourists for short-term stays.

sections.label: Airbnb legalised in London
sections.summary: In London, Airbnb was legalised in March 2015, allowing home owners to rent out their places for up to three months a year with certain conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In London, Airbnb was legalised in March 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, home owners can rent out their places for up to three months a year, with certain conditions attached, of course.

sections.label: Third party taxi booking framework
sections.summary: A basic regulatory framework was introduced last year requiring all third party taxi booking services to comply with certain conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: A basic regulatory framework was introduced last year where all third party taxi booking services are required to comply with certain conditions.

sections.label: Reviewing regulations for commuter safety
sections.summary: The Government is reviewing further regulations, with the aim of commuter safety rather than inconveniencing commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Government is still reviewing the need for further regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: But at the end of the day, the desire to even out the playing field must be for the safety of the commuters rather than inconveniencing the commuters − like making them wait 15 minutes before they can get onto an Uber taxi, which has been the case in Paris since 2013.

sections.label: MRT disruptions in 2015
sections.summary: In 2015 there was a spate of MRT disruptions in February and March and the worst in MRT history in July.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, in 2015, we saw a spate of MRT disruptions in February and March, as well as the worst disruption in the history of the MRT in July.

sections.label: Hawker centre stall costs in Yishun
sections.summary: A new hawker centre stall costs $5,000 rental plus $1,680 cleaning, and the speaker hopes NEA works with the community in Yishun.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To the man-on-the-street, a hawker centre is the place to get good food at a reasonable price.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But how can the price be reasonable if the hawker has to pay $6,000 for his stall?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To be exact, I was told by the taxi-drivers who live in Nee Soon South, it is $5,000 rental plus $1,680 for cleaning services and this is charged in a new hawker centre.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And the Yishun residents do not just hope to have good food at reasonable prices, many also hope to get a stall to provide them with employment.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope that NEA is open to the concept of working with the community, perhaps with the social enterprises, to operate the new hawker centre in Yishun.

sections.label: Littering fines, smoking, Nee Soon South
sections.summary: Littering fines were the highest in six years, smoking is rising, and 50 smoking points will extend the Nee Soon South programme.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, the amount from fines for littering was the highest in six years.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our smoking rate is gradually going back up.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Designated Smoking Point scheme piloted in Nee Soon South has achieved its desired outcome.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This year, we will build 50 smoking points and extend the programme to the entire Nee Soon South.

sections.label: Work Permit loss for layoffs
sections.summary: With the slowest job growth in 13 years, the speaker asks if a company laying off Singaporeans should lose Work Permits.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to MOM's report this morning, last year, we witnessed the slowest job growth in 13 years.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider that each time a company lays off a Singaporean worker, it will subsequently lose a Work Permit?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If a company lays off one Singaporean, it will lose one Work Permit; if it lays off two, it will lose two Work Permits.

sections.label: SkillsFuture lifelong scholarships for citizens
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore gives free lifelong scholarships to everyone through SkillsFuture so people can upgrade themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We evolve, as hon Member Mr Ong Ye Kung had described so poetically on Monday, "to adapt to the changing global environment".

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We have to be the first country in the world which gives free lifelong scholarships to everyone through SkillsFuture – I call it scholarship, no other country I have heard of so far is giving this scholarship to every citizen – so that our people can upgrade themselves while pursuing their interests and passions.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and Government care
sections.summary: SkillsFuture is how the Government takes care of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture is the way the Government takes care of Singaporeans.

sections.label: SkillsFuture keeps Singaporeans competitive
sections.summary: SkillsFuture will let Singaporeans stay relevant and ahead of competition throughout their lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture will enable Singaporeans to stay relevant and ahead of competition throughout their lives.

sections.label: Foreign investment and growth clusters
sections.summary: Foreign investment and free trade remain needed, and MOF and MTI announced measures and growth clusters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We will continue to need foreign investment and promote free trade with other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I am glad that MOF had announced in its Addendum that the Government will be putting in measures to transform our economy from one which focused on value-adding to value-creating, to develop innovative and differentiated products and services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MTI's Addendum also listed out the Advanced Manufacturing, Logistics & Aerospace, Biomedical Sciences and Smart & Sustainable Urban Solutions Growth Clusters which it will be focusing on.

sections.label: SME business costs review
sections.summary: The speaker supports SCCCI's call for a cost review committee on rising business costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to speak on our SMEs, particularly, the need to reduce business costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I support the recent call by the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI) to set up a cost review committee to look into the main contributors to rising business costs.

sections.label: SMEs, foreign worker levies
sections.summary: SMEs employ 70% of the workforce, and levies are unnecessary given existing foreign worker quotas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Remember that our SMEs employ 70% of our workforce and their survival is critical to their employees and their families who depend upon them for their livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As we have already in place quotas for foreign workers in every sector, the levies are unnecessary as a mechanism to regulate demand by businesses.

sections.label: SMEs global market and Special Employment Credit
sections.summary: SMEs need an edge globally, and the speaker hopes the Special Employment Credit doubles from 3% to 6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our SMEs need the edge to break through to the global market as our domestic market is too small.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also hope the Government will double the Special Employment Credit from 3% to 6% to support workers above 65 years old who wish to work.

sections.label: PPHS temporary flats births
sections.summary: More than 100 babies were born to couples living in the first batch of 1,150 temporary flats under the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: More than 100 babies were born to couples living in the first batch of 1,150 temporary flats under the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS).

sections.label: Singaporeans living in HDB flats
sections.summary: More than 80% of Singaporeans live in HDB flats and many are proud owners of their HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: More than 80% of Singaporeans live in HDB flats and many Singaporeans are proud to be owners of their HDB flats.

sections.label: HDB flat pricing and ECs
sections.summary: A speaker hopes the Government will delink new HDB flat prices from the open market, extend the Lease Buyback Scheme and regulate EC prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Many who want to sell their properties now face the dilemma of reducing prices to sell their house, or face the pressure of falling prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There must be continuation of good policies and I hope that the Government will continue to delink the prices of new HDB flats from the open market and use the average annual salary of Singaporeans as the basis for determining prices, so as to ensure that Singaporeans and their descendants will not have to worry and that they will always be able to own a flat that they can afford.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is to encourage Singaporeans to manage their finances and not over leverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also hope that this term of Government will consider extending the Lease Buyback Scheme to bigger flats and not just 4-room and smaller flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On executive condominiums (ECs), I also hope that the Government will consider regulating the prices of ECs and use the pricing model of new flats as a basis to determine the prices of ECs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This will prevent the re-emergence of a bubble in our property market.

sections.label: Foreigner property sales and singles
sections.summary: A speaker agrees with Australia's measures against foreign property speculation and hopes the Government will bear in mind singles' twilight years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   I also agree with my fellow Parliamentary colleagues with regard to Australia's measures to prevent property speculation by foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: We can follow the example of Australia, whereby foreigners, including permanent residents, can only sell their houses to Australians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: In terms of the design of 2-room flats provided for singles, I also hope that the Government will bear in mind the needs of these singles during their twilight years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: I support HDB's policy of co- Page: 78 locating 2-room flats with other flat types within a block of flats.

sections.label: Opposition party and political reform
sections.summary: A speaker agrees with the Prime Minister's political reform proposals and says they will meet the country's needs and Singaporeans' expectations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: They also want an ideal and reliable Opposition party in Parliament, to have more voices in Parliament without affecting the Government's efficiency or crippling the administration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Therefore, I agree with the Prime Minister's political reform proposals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: They will be able to meet the needs of the country and expectations of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As the last new Member of this House to speak, let me first start by saying that I am humbled, we all are humbled and honoured to be given this opportunity to serve this House, to serve Singapore and to serve Singaporeans.

sections.label: Debating morals and Singaporeans' aspirations
sections.summary: A speaker calls for more discussion and debate about morals and ethics and about Singaporeans' dreams, hopes and aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Let us also discuss and debate even more about the morals and ethics, about Singaporeans' dreams, hopes and aspirations, more Page: 79 about the heart of the matter.

sections.label: Animal cruelty and human-animal conflicts
sections.summary: The passage calls for fighting animal cruelty and finding humane long-term solutions to human-animal conflicts in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Let us ensure that we fight animal cruelty and we find humane long-term solutions to the human-animal conflicts in Singapore.

sections.label: Humane policies, environment and reducing
sections.summary: It urges humane, scientifically justifiable policies, moral obligation for a sustainable future, and focus on Reuse and Reduce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The very essence of being human is being humane.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need to ensure that the policies we implement address both residents' and animal welfare concerns and are scientifically justifiable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: When we talk about the environment and climate change, let us not only focus on the economic losses due to climate change, not just the monetary values of trees and the ecosystem, but focus on our moral obligation to ensure a sustainable future for all and the intrinsic value of our trees and ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need to focus not only on recycling but also, more importantly, the other Rs, Reuse and, most importantly, Reduce.

sections.label: Baby Bonus Scheme child-raising costs
sections.summary: The speaker says she understands child-raising costs in Singapore and that the Baby Bonus Scheme has been useful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I fully understand, appreciate and am experiencing the costs involved in bringing up a child in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, the Baby Bonus Scheme, which helps to lighten the financial costs of raising children, has been very useful.

sections.label: Childcare leave based on number of children
sections.summary: The speaker supports flexi-work after maternity leave and wants childcare leave based on the number of children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I support what Mr Desmond Choo had earlier said about more flexi-working hour arrangements following maternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope we can also relook our childcare leave policies, leave policies and base the amount of leave not just on the age of the children but also the number of children one has.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Quite simply, the more children you have, the more childcare leave you should have.

sections.label: Volunteer programme for lower income families
sections.summary: A new volunteer-planned, volunteer-run and volunteer-funded programme in Nee Soon East aims to help lower income families out of poverty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the help of the community, we can do more and do more to ensure that these families can get out of the poverty cycle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We have launched a new programme for our lower income families in Nee Soon East where I serve and I am glad that more and more people are stepping forward to help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The beauty of the programme is that it is planned by volunteers, run by volunteers and funded by volunteers.

sections.label: Unconventional career and ACRES charity
sections.summary: The speaker says her unconventional career and charity ACRES were possible despite sceptics, showing nothing is impossible in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this island where the impossible has been achieved, my choice of pursuing an unconventional career 15 years ago has been made possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many sceptics laughed at me 15 years ago when I started my charity ACRES, when I told them I was going to become an activist, an advocate for change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They told me that I would fail, that this is not something feasible to establish and sustain in Singapore and that I would not be able to engage, empower, inspire and mobilise anyone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And so, if there is one lesson I have learnt in the past 15 years, it is that nothing is truly impossible in Singapore.

sections.label: Building Singapore as home
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Singapore remains a treasured home and that each person plays a part in building a stronger Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that "Home" is not just a song we sing at events but that Singapore continues to be a place we call our home, a place we treasure and a place we build up for our children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope we leave behind a legacy of compassion, of giving, of hope for a stronger Singapore as we move towards SG100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And it reads, "I am only one but still I am one, I cannot do everything but still I can do something.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And because I cannot do everything, I will not refuse to do the something that I can do." Each one of us has that part to play, an important part to do something and, together, we can make Singapore even better, even stronger and even more beautiful.

sections.label: Diverse society, 47,000 views
sections.summary: With a more diverse society and complex global environment, Singaporeans should move forward as one people, after hearing views from some 47,000 Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: As a more diverse society emerges and with a more complex global environment to navigate, we should put our heads together, to take things forward as one people.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We heard from some 47,000 Singaporeans, expressing views on matters concerning our livelihood, such as job opportunities and housing.

sections.label: Democracy of deeds, SGfuture
sections.summary: All hands are needed for challenges ahead, and a democracy of deeds underlies the SGfuture engagements launched last November.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: As Minister Grace Fu said last week, we need all hands on deck to face the challenges ahead.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We want to build a democracy of deeds, where Singaporeans have a greater sense of ownership, responsibility and a greater connection to what it means to be Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: That is the premise behind the SGfuture engagements launched last November.

sections.label: SG50 and democracy of deeds
sections.summary: SG50 renewed a sense that Singaporeans want to be involved, so the democracy of deeds will be integral to this term of Government.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: But SG50 has given us a renewed sense that Singaporeans want to be involved.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: This democracy of deeds will therefore be an integral part of this term of Government.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The SGfuture engagements give a glimpse into how we are intending to do so by matching ideas with action and people with projects.

sections.label: Hope Centre bread and tuition
sections.summary: Hope Centre runs monthly bread distribution to rental flat residents in Tampines North and is planning free tuition for needy families' children.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Increasingly, I see offers to get involved, for example, the Hope Centre's monthly bread distribution to rental flat residents in Tampines North which started last year.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Hope Centre and Tampines North grassroots organisations are now discussing and planning for a new free tuition service for children of needy families.

sections.label: Arts and Culture Strategic Review
sections.summary: Over three years, the Arts and Culture Strategic Review has seen increased funding, with more arts groups and talents benefiting.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Over the last three years, with the Arts and Culture Strategic Review, we have not only seen increased funding but also more arts groups and talents in the arts community are benefiting from this funding.

sections.label: Conditions on productivity and sports support
sections.summary: The Productivity and Innovation Credit for companies and sports scholarships for athletes come with conditions in employment and training and performance.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: For example, the Productivity and Innovation Credit that helps companies raise productivity comes with conditions in employment.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Sports scholarship for our athletes comes with conditions in training and in performance.

sections.label: MPs heading NSAs and FAS
sections.summary: The Ministry does not appoint MPs to head NSAs, except FAS, whose president was appointed by the Minister responsible for Sports; FAS is moving to member elections by June.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The Ministry does not appoint Members of Parliament to head NSAs.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The only exception today is the Football Association of Singapore (FAS) where the President of FAS has been appointed by the Minister responsible for Sports.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: FAS is transiting to a system of election by members.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: By June, an AGM will be called during which members will elect their next president.

sections.label: Long-time PRs and FAS elections
sections.summary: A speaker asks for special consideration for long-time PRs from Malaysia in citizenship applications and welcomes confirmation that FAS council members will be elected.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: They have done their part as good member of the Singapore society and the Singapore community.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope the Government can give this group of long-time PRs from Malaysia special consideration and concession in their citizenship application.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He spoke in his speech about leadership of sports groups and also referred to what I had said earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am glad to hear his confirmation for the association where the Government is nominating all the council members, in other words, in the Football Association of Singapore, that that is being changed and now they would have an election.

sections.label: MPs leading national sports associations
sections.summary: Eight NSAs currently have MPs in leadership, and the Government neither bans politicians from NSAs nor requires MPs to lead them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: As I mentioned, currently, there are only eight NSAs with Members of Parliament at their leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: The Government does not ban politicians from entering NSAs nor dictate that the leadership must be helmed by Members in this Chamber.

sections.label: NAC funding conditions for arts groups
sections.summary: NAC funding requires arts groups not to put public institutions in a bad light, and a funding reconsideration followed a change in the works' content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: As part of the funding principles of NAC, there is a requirement and understanding with the arts groups and the applicants that they should not put any public institutions in a bad light or put them in a derogatory position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: It is in this context that was quoted by Arts Engage that the funding was re-considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: But also, there was a change in substance of the content of the works that were first submitted for application and the eventual product that was produced by the artist.

sections.label: Select Committees in parliamentary democracies
sections.summary: Select Committees meeting when Parliament is not in session are fundamental pillars, and Erskine May notes they have become the principal scrutiny mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, Select Committees that meet regularly when Parliament is not session are fundamental pillars of many parliamentary democracies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Erskine May on parliamentary procedures, the signature reference book used by parliaments in the Commonwealth, including Singapore, notes that Select Committees "have over recent years become the principal mechanism by which the House discharges its responsibility for the scrutiny of Government policy and actions".

sections.label: Hong Kong Legislative Council panels
sections.summary: The Hong Kong Legislative Council has 18 panels that deliberate on policy areas and give views on major proposals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Hong Kong Legislative Council hosts 18 different panels to deliberate on issues relating to specific policy areas and also to give views on major legislative or financial proposals before their formal introduction to the Council or the Finance Committee.

sections.label: Elderly Singaporeans doubling
sections.summary: The number of elderly Singaporeans is expected to double in the next decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, there is a prospect of a Singapore where the number of elderly Singaporeans is expected to double in the next decade.

sections.label: Population policy mid-course review
sections.summary: The Government announced a mid-course population policy review around 2020, which a Population Select Committee could start hearing early.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, there is a difficult population policy issue for which the Government has announced a mid-course review to take place around 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Population Select Committee could potentially start hearings on this issue early, allowing Singaporeans to understand the decisions taken thus far and outline what other policies need to dovetail closely with our population strategies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It could also flesh out the different perspectives of Singaporeans with regard to trade-offs between the dwindling Singaporean Core and the economic strategies required for Singapore not just to survive, but to thrive in the next lap.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Select Committee proposal
sections.summary: Singapore has not met productivity aims, so a SkillsFuture Select Committee of MPs from all parties is proposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Even in Singapore, we have not achieved the productivity aims set in the Economic Strategies Committee Report 2020 of 2%-3% each year, and our numbers continue to look weak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As productivity and the acquisition of new skills are closely linked, a SkillsFuture Select Committee of Parliament comprising Members of Parliament from all parties would be in a good position to pursue and consider improvements and innovations to the Government strategies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This would ensure that SkillsFuture would work well on the ground, and examine how it could do more and to account for the taxpayer dollar that is eventually expended on it.

sections.label: Employment growth and layoffs
sections.summary: MOM estimates show unemployment stayed low but employment growth slowed to a 12-year low and 4,200 workers were laid off.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: According to preliminary estimates released by MOM, while the unemployment rate in Singapore remained low last year, total employment growth slowed to a 12-year low.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Redundancy increased in the fourth quarter of 2015, as 4,200 workers were laid off.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This was higher than the previous quarter and the year before.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum's "The Future of Jobs" report that was issued this month outlined that these changes are not unique to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It highlighted that "many of the drivers of major transformation currently affecting global industries are expected to have significant impact on jobs, ranging from significant job creation to job displacement and from heightened labour productivity to widening skills gap." While we must have strategies to ensure that Singapore continues to have good growth and quality jobs, what is equally important will be to ensure that Singaporeans are able and more importantly, ready to take advantage of these job opportunities and that businesses in Singapore are also able to fill these jobs with the right talent.

sections.label: Strengthening Singapore Core workforce
sections.summary: Strengthening the Singapore Core in the workforce is important, and employers must play a big role.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As outlined by MOM in the Addendum, strengthening this Singapore Core in the workforce in very important.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I believe that given that Singapore has a highly educated workforce with more than 50% holding PMET jobs, this trend will continue to increase and, so, we must have high-quality jobs that Singaporeans aspire to do and can do.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What must we do to achieve this, apart from the measures that MOM is driving?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I believe that employers must play a big role for a strong Singapore Core to be successful.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It will require employers to be willing to make a deliberate bet on building a Singapore Core.

sections.label: Employers, workers, educational institutions using skills
sections.summary: The speaker urges employers, workers and educational institutions to use existing requirements and refine them to build a strong Singapore Core.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I encourage employers, workers, educational institutions to leverage and use these.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I must say that while I do applaud the involvement of Select Committees to do this, I think what is more important now is for us to exercise what is there so that businesses, individuals and associations and educational institutions will be able to knock out the kinks to see what those requirements are, to further refine it so that we can really build up that skills base that is required for our workers to be really strong and to really build a Singapore Core.

sections.label: Tapping more highly educated women
sections.summary: The speaker says women are more highly educated now and should be tapped.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In fact, the women are more highly educated now, so do tap on the women as well.

sections.label: Mature PMEs and Singapore Core
sections.summary: The speaker calls for bringing young and mature PME talent together to build a strong Singapore Core.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: And I am not talking about just the graduating workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We have a very, very precious workforce called the middle-age or the mature PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: When you bring that diversity of talent together, both young and old, you will see the impact that will bring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Therefore, I do encourage all of us to go forward to build that Singapore Core.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In order to future-ready and build a strong Singapore Core in our workforce, I implore all of us to work together.

sections.label: Reviewing Elected Presidency qualifications
sections.summary: The speaker says the Elected Presidency qualification criteria should be reviewed and the President's role clarified as non-political.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Elected Presidency, for instance, it is appropriate that the qualification criteria is reviewed because many changes have taken place, including the administration of the state institution, while the size of national reserves have also changed since the system of Elected President was introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We have to be responsible in ensuring stability, because when a leadership change occurs in the Government, we will need sufficient safeguards to ensure that any government, regardless of which party it is, will act responsibly when making key appointments and in the protection of reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The role of the President has undergone many changes, not only as the Head of State who represents Singapore's interests, but also as the guardian of the national reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must use this review process to further highlight the actual role of the Elected President, and the people need to recognise and understand the President's functions and powers, that is, the President's role is not imbued with political power, and he does not play a role in developing policy initiatives.

sections.label: Review and minority President candidate
sections.summary: The speaker says a review is needed and the Malay community welcomes a minority candidate provision for the Elected President.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, a review needs to be done to make this institution more relevant and able to constantly meet future needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am sure that the Malay community welcomes the considerations made to provide for a minority candidate for the office of the Elected President.

sections.label: No Malay President since Yusof Ishak
sections.summary: Singapore has not had a Malay President since Encik Yusof Ishak in 1970, over 45 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singapore had not had a Malay President since the late Encik Yusof Ishak in 1970, which is over 45 years ago.

sections.label: Constitutional Commission qualifying criteria revision
sections.summary: The Constitutional Commission's revision of qualifying criteria is timely as state institutions and reserves have grown more complex since 1990.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The revision of the qualifying criteria by the Constitutional Commission is timely – it was 25 years ago since they were drawn in 1990 – as the complexity of safeguarding our state institutions and reserves has gone up in magnitude since then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, in 1990, the Temasek Net Portfolio Value was S$10 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As of March last year, this amount has grown by more than 25 times to S$266 billion.

sections.label: No Malay President since 1970
sections.summary: Singapore has not had a Malay President since Mr Ishak in 1970, almost 46 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In fact, we have not had a Malay President in Singapore since Mr Ishak, in 1970, almost 46 years ago.

sections.label: PAP expands NCMP scheme
sections.summary: After winning a strong mandate, the PAP Government expanded the NCMP scheme by 25% instead of keeping the status quo.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Many I spoke to were surprised that after winning a strong mandate from the people of Singapore last year, the PAP Government could have easily kept the status quo, ensuring that Singaporeans can afford to continue to vote a PAP Government and yet have diversity in Parliament through the existing NCMP scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But yet, it has opened the competition wider by expanding the NCMP scheme by as much as 25% in the spirit of having greater debate in Parliament.

sections.label: NCMP position respect and replacement
sections.summary: The NCMP position has been given more respect and dignity, and parties cannot assume entitlement to offer it to other candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Given the increased voting privileges to the NCMP, I would like to point out that the position is one that has been given more respect and dignity and not turned down so easily for replacement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Parties cannot also assume that just because one of its candidates turned down the offer of being an NCMP, that it is their entitlement to offer it to anyone of their other candidates.

sections.label: NCMP vacancies and security threats
sections.summary: Vacant NCMP seats should only be considered for replacement at a by-election, as the Government faces heightened terrorism and ISIS threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If we want to take the NCMP system seriously, we should treat it like any seat left vacant by a constituency Member of Parliament moving forward, any seat that is left vacant should only be considered for replacement should there be a by-election before the next General Elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Increasingly, the Government will have to grapple with heightened terrorist activities and the rise of ISIS in Southeast Asia, as well as the possibility of Islamophobia and increased religious tensions.

sections.label: Roundtable model for social harmony
sections.summary: The Government sometimes gets caught in between, and this model should change into a roundtable where each group is an equal partner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In doing so, sometimes, the Government gets caught in between and, thus, has to calibrate its intervention and relationships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This model should change into a roundtable where each group is an equal partner and a stakeholder to the social harmony and stability.

sections.label: Inter-racial and inter-religious task force
sections.summary: A Member asks the Government to form a task force of diverse religious and racial groups to strengthen inter-racial and inter-religious ties and recalibrate policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Given this "new normal", it may now be a good time to recalibrate and also sense where each of the other faiths are with all these difficult issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would ask the Government to establish a task force, made up of members of diverse religious and racial groups, to study and recommend appropriate mechanisms to strengthen this inter-racial and inter-religious fabric, as well as discuss areas where we need to recalibrate our policies to accommodate new developments or requirements of different faiths, areas that other respective faiths are also prepared to accept.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Today, these fixtures are illegal when these are installed at public spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, during the last General Elections, campaigning by certain candidates took a religious tone and I was surprised that the Elections Department did not intervene or come out with a warning sooner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is probably because it did not lead to any open conflict, which the Parliamentary Election rules specify as a premise for intervention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But when candidates start to campaign along religious lines, what does this indicate about our political landscape?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It has been seen in many countries that religion and state can be hard to separate and once we go down that path, away from the open and secular spaces that we have built after decades of Independence, there may be a point of no return.

sections.label: Sitting suspended, maiden speeches
sections.summary: The sitting was suspended from 4.00 pm to 4.20 pm, and the new Members' maiden speeches were congratulated.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.00 pm until 4.20 pm.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I appreciate the thoughtful points raised and congratulate the new Members on their maiden speeches.

sections.label: Creating and sharing value
sections.summary: It states that value must be created for the world and ourselves to survive, and that value must be shared so we can be our best.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, we need to continue creating value for the world and for ourselves, if we are to make a living and survive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, the value that we create, we must share, in a way that lets us continue to be our best.

sections.label: Growth of global digital data
sections.summary: Global digital data usage doubles every two years, and by 2020 the digital universe will grow 50-fold from 2010.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Global digital data usage is doubling every two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: By 2020, the size of the digital universe will increase 50-fold from 2010.

sections.label: National Innovation Challenge on Ageing
sections.summary: The National Innovation Challenge on Ageing crowdsourced over 100 proposals on home-care, healthy lifespans and ageless workplaces, which were evaluated and good ideas will be acted on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Last year, the National Innovation Challenge on Ageing crowdsourced solutions in areas like better home-care, increasing healthy lifespans and creating ageless workplaces.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We got over 100 good proposals and these have been evaluated and the good ideas will be put into action.

sections.label: Social policy innovations studied worldwide
sections.summary: Singapore's social policy innovations in CPF, HDB, healthcare, social safety nets and the Pioneer Generation Package are studied by people around the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our social policy innovations in CPF, HDB, healthcare, social safety nets and the Pioneer Generation Package are studied by people around the world.

sections.label: Chinatown library no staff
sections.summary: The Chinatown library is a public library that has no staff.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: One inspiring example which I learnt recently is our Chinatown library.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: It is a public library with no staff.

sections.label: Library user satisfaction rates
sections.summary: It has one of the highest user satisfaction rates of all libraries in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Best of all, of all libraries in Singapore, it has one of the highest user satisfaction rates.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and healthcare plans
sections.summary: SkillsFuture enables lifelong learning, the Pioneer Generation Package cares for pioneers, MediShield Life provides risk-pooling, and preventive and primary care is the next healthcare area.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: One very significant innovation that we are embarking on is SkillsFuture, which will enable our people, regardless of age, regardless of professions, to continue learning all their life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Pioneer Generation Package takes care of our pioneers, while MediShield Life provides for risk-pooling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The next major area in healthcare would be preventive and primary care, as set out in the MOH Addendum.

sections.label: Students swim record laps
sections.summary: Students swam 7,505 laps within one hour, almost double the old record set by adults.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our students swam to a new record of 7,505 laps within one hour, almost double the old record set by adults.

sections.label: SG50 Care and Share volunteers
sections.summary: Over 200,000 volunteers joined the SG50 Care and Share movement, which sought to rally Singaporeans to share.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: When we were planning SG50, we sought to rally Singaporeans to share.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I am delighted that over 200,000 volunteers came onboard our SG50 Care and Share movement.

sections.label: Objective for Singapore's future
sections.summary: The objective is to keep Singapore prosperous and stable and improve lives of succeeding generations, by creating value, shaping the future and sharing value together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our objective is very clear: to keep Singapore prosperous and stable, and improve the lives of succeeding generations of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In order to achieve our objective, we must create value together, shape our future together and share value amongst Singaporeans.

sections.label: Education as gift for children
sections.summary: Education is described as the best gift for each child, and every child should have a chance to succeed regardless of family background.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Education is the best gift that we can give to each child.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Every child, regardless of family background, should have a chance to succeed.

sections.label: Building Singapore for dreams
sections.summary: The purpose stated is to build a Singapore where every Singaporean can reach their dreams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The "what for" is this: to build a Singapore where every Singaporean can reach our dreams.

sections.label: Terrorism attacks and Singapore arrests
sections.summary: Jakarta, Paris, Istanbul and Beirut were hit by terrorism recently, and 27 radicalised individuals were arrested in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Just in the last few months alone, Jakarta, Paris, Istanbul and Beirut were hit by terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The recent arrest of 27 radicalised individuals right here in Singapore is a sobering reminder of this new reality.

sections.label: Committee on Future Economy and SkillsFuture
sections.summary: The Committee on the Future Economy, led by Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat, shows government emphasis on economic strategies, with SkillsFuture preparing workers to re-skill and up-skill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The formation of the Committee on the Future Economy, helmed by our Finance Minister, Mr Heng Swee Keat whom we just listened to, shows the Government's emphasis in developing economic strategies that will position Singapore well for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With the SkillsFuture initiative, we should be ready for a future economy where workers are empowered to re-skill, up-skill, allowing us to develop a strong Singaporean Core in the workplace, issues raised by Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar, Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Heng Chee How.

sections.label: SMEs and startups as innovation source
sections.summary: Dr Koh Poh Koon, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Leon Perera pointed that SMEs and startups, especially high-growth ones, are an important source of innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Dr Koh Poh Koon, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Leon Perera pointed that SMEs and startups, especially those with high growth potential, are an important source of innovation in our economy.

sections.label: Senior care and active ageing ideas
sections.summary: Dr Amy Khor and Miss Cheng Li Hui mooted co-locating senior care centres at community clubs, active ageing hubs in new HDB developments, and multi-generational neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For our seniors, innovative ideas like co-locating senior care centres at community clubs and planning for active ageing hubs in new HDB developments as well as the planning for multi-generational neighbourhoods were mooted by Dr Amy Khor and Miss Cheng Li Hui respectively.

sections.label: Coordinating Minister for Economic and Social policies
sections.summary: Creating a Coordinating Minister for Economic and Social policies reflects the Government's emphasis on aligning social policies with economic policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The creation of a Coordinating Minister for Economic and Social policies, Deputy Prime Minister Tharman, reflects the Government's emphasis on aligning our social policies with those of our economic policies, for our economic policies must meet our social needs.

sections.label: Transformation of public housing and communities
sections.summary: Members said transformation should involve better and more affordable public housing, more green spaces, long-term infrastructural plans and harnessing technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As highlighted by several Members including Dr Teo Ho Pin, Mr Lim Biow Chuan, Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mr Ong Teng Koon, this transformation should involve building better and more affordable public housing, creating more green spaces within our communities, embarking in long-term infrastructural plans to support a changing population, and harnessing technology and its potential benefits.

sections.label: SGfuture dialogues and Committee on the Future Economy
sections.summary: The President highlighted two national platforms, the SGfuture dialogues and the Committee on the Future Economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Moving forward, the President has highlighted two national platforms, namely the SGfuture dialogues and the Committee on the Future Economy.

sections.label: NCMP seats and constitutional voting rights
sections.summary: The speaker says increasing NCMP seats to 12 with constitutional voting rights assures more voices and diverse views in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Stay united, work hard and embrace the pioneering spirit of our forefathers." The vehicle to which these five aims will be delivered is a decisive, stable and reliable Government, one that is effective and leads by example, and that introduces well-crafted and effective initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In my view, an increase in the seats of NCMPs to 12 and equipping them with constitutional voting rights, provide assurance of more voices in Parliament, more diverse views and, consequently, a greater need to persuade, placed on the Government's shoulders.

sections.label: Refining political system and mentorship
sections.summary: The Prime Minister outlined refinements to make the political system more robust and responsive, while the speaker stressed not discarding continuity of mentorship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister outlined how the Government will be making the necessary refinements to the current system to make our political system more robust and responsive to the changing political landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Starting politics at a young age, I had to learn humbly and fast, and more than anything, it taught me the importance and value of mentorship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, while we tweaked and refined the system, let us not throw out the continuity of mentorship, especially in the ecosystem of politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The value of mentorship from more experienced Ministers, Members, senior leaders, the imparting of values, and the training of reflex actions to make important decisions in crisis situations must never be sidelined.

sections.label: Continuity of mentorship
sections.summary: The passage states the need to ensure continuity of mentorship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: You need IQ because the margin of error for Singapore is very small." The need to ensure continuity of mentorship.

sections.label: Four areas and senior leaders
sections.summary: The content covers four areas, and the speaker asks to preserve long paths for senior leaders to impart values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The content invariably revolves around four areas: one, how can we better the lives of Singaporeans; two, how we should never be afraid of breaking out of outdated mind sets; three, how we each play a part in advancing Singapore; and four, very importantly, how are our constituents?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The store of experience in the Prime Minister and his senior colleagues is immense.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While we tweak and refine the political institutions and the landscape, I ask because I believe this to be important, that we preserve the model of having long paths for senior leaders to impart values and lessons even after they decide to leave apex or active leadership positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There is much value for Singapore to reap, provided Singaporeans and their advancement always remain the focus of political energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Let us respect the precious trust that has been placed in our hands by the constituents we serve.
